caption:
Anthropic's stock fell 7.4% on Tuesday and slipped below its $83 IPO price, less than a week after its debut.
On day one it briefly hit $115. SpaceX took more than a month to fall below its own IPO price.
Nvidia and other AI stocks tumbled too, as investors doubt AI can pay for all those data centers.

paragraphs.text: Anthropic shares fell below their initial public offering price on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. The Associated Press reported that the stock dropped 7.4% by midday to below $83, the price at which the company sold shares in its IPO the previous week.

Fast Company reported that the stock traded as low as $81.40 before the market opened on November 24. On its first day of trading, Anthropic had briefly climbed as high as about $115, according to both outlets, before giving up much of that gain.
A short run above the offer price

Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq on November 19, 2026, under the ticker ANT. Futurism reported that the debut gave the company a market value of more than $1.3 trillion, well short of the roughly $2 trillion that had been expected. Fast Company described the offering as an $81.3 billion IPO, larger than the $75 billion SpaceX raised in its own record listing.

According to Fast Company, the shares fell sharply on Friday, the day after the debut, and stayed mostly below $90 from then on. They rallied on Monday, November 23, a move the outlet linked to the surprise news that Jensen Huang would return as chief executive of Nvidia.

The slide below the offer price came quickly by recent standards. SpaceX listed on June 12, 2026, at $135 a share and did not trade below that level until July 15, more than a month later, Fast Company noted.

Anthropic was not alone. The AP reported that Nvidia fell 7.1% on November 24, one day after a 31.5% jump that was its biggest gain in more than two decades. CoreWeave dropped 11.6% and GE Vernova lost 4.6%. As of 12:41 p.m. Eastern time, the Nasdaq composite was down 1.3% and the S&P 500 was down 0.3%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 0.9%.

The AP said the main concern among investors is that AI stocks rose too far into a possible bubble. It cited doubts that AI will produce enough profit and productivity to justify heavy spending on data centers, high interest rates that make borrowing more expensive, and worries that Democratic gains in the midterm elections could bring tighter rules on AI, including possible pauses in data center construction. Fast Company pointed to similar fears about overvaluation and spending.

Futurism noted that Anthropic's own numbers give investors plenty to weigh. The company grew revenue about twelvefold in 2025 but lost $42 billion that year, according to the outlet, and its prospectus lists among its risks the possibility that AI could pose catastrophic or existential dangers.

For a company that set a record with its listing, trading below the offer price within a week is a sign that public investors are pricing Anthropic like the rest of the AI trade rather than as a special case. The stock moved with Nvidia and CoreWeave on November 24, which suggests the drop says more about the market's mood toward AI spending than about any single piece of Anthropic news.

A fall below the IPO price also matters for the banks that ran the offering and for other AI companies weighing their own listings. Investors who bought at $83 are now holding a loss, and that can make the next large AI offering harder to price.
The next test is whether Anthropic can close back above $83 in the coming sessions, and whether Nvidia, which moved the whole AI group on November 23 and 24, steadies or keeps swinging.
